stem:
Lavanya helps with three problems: an ant bite that stings from formic acid, soil that tests acidic, and factory wastewater that tests strongly basic before discharge.

Which set of actions correctly uses opposite natures?

options.text: Baking soda paste on the bite, lime on the acidic soil, and a carefully controlled acid treatment of the basic wastewater after testing.
Add baking soda to all factory wastewater before discharge, without first checking whether each batch is acidic or basic.
Add organic matter to the acidic soil to correct its acidity.
Leave neutral soil without any nutrient care forever, because neutral soil never needs fertiliser.

teacher.key_rationale: Remedies must oppose the identified condition: base for acidic bite/soil, acid for basic waste. Universal baking soda omits diagnosis; organic matter suits basic soil, so using it on acidic soil reverses the relation; claiming neutral soil never needs fertiliser over-extends the scope.
